findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add a one-line comment fix to decide.py in this change's scope (a comment-only touch does not violate the stated intent), or add an explicit follow-up ticket reference so the stale comment is not silently left behind.
evidence: "note decide.py's inline comment misattributes this pin to test_impact_plan.py, which pins only UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB; the plan cites the real pin"
Plan explicitly identifies the comment is wrong but then excludes decide.py from the change scope.
findings.finding: The plan explicitly identifies a stale inline comment in decide.py (it misattributes the INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB pin to test_impact_plan.py when the real pin is in test_divergence_grade_split.py), but declares decide.py NOT touched — leaving a known-incorrect code comment persisting in a high-traffic kernel file.
findings.location: Approach section (3), decide.py inline comment misattribution note; Scope section 'NOT touched: src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py'
scenarios: A future developer reading decide.py's inline comment is directed to test_impact_plan.py for the INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB pin, finds no such pin there, and is confused about the actual constraint.
A reviewer auditing the pin coverage trusts the comment and checks the wrong test file, potentially missing the real constraint in test_divergence_grade_split.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Add decide.py to the scope for a comment-only fix: change the misattributed reference from `test_impact_plan.py` to `test_divergence_grade_split.py:142` in the inline comment. Alternatively, note `# TODO(this-ticket): comment misattributes pin — see test_divergence_grade_split.py:142` to flag it without a functional change.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback path (e.g., 'to revert: restore G7 entry in criteria_routing.json to block_threshold 0.95 / default_posture advisory and update the three pinned test assertions') so the behavioral change satisfies T4's reversibility requirement.
evidence: 'Routing (criteria_routing.json, G7 entry): block_threshold 0.95 -> 0.85, default_posture advisory -> blocking'
'Monitoring note (explicitly NOT an acceptance criterion): re-run the FP classification once >= 20 kind-graded G7 findings have accumulated'
No section describes a revert procedure or expand-contract sequencing if blocking produces unexpected FP spikes after deployment
T4 rubric: 'acknowledgement alone is insufficient; require the reversibility mechanism'
findings.finding: The plan changes G7's default_posture from 'advisory' to 'blocking' — an explicit behavioral change that will cause previously-advisory G7 findings to block plan merges — but provides no explicit rollback or back-out path. The Monitoring note defers recheck but does not constitute a reversibility mechanism.
scenarios: A wave of G7 floor-kind findings blocks several legitimate plans before the 20-finding monitoring threshold is reached; with no documented rollback, the team must reconstruct the revert steps under pressure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-paragraph 'Rollback' section: 'To revert this change, restore the G7 entry in criteria_routing.json to {block_threshold: 0.95, default_posture: "advisory"}, update EXPECTED_ROUTING and G7_BLOCKING in test_threshold_recalibration.py back to (0.95, "advisory"), remove G7 from _PLAN_REVIEW_APPROVED_BLOCKING, and restore test_g7_posture_is_advisory_at_0_95 in test_plan_review_g7.py. Because the change is purely config + rubric text, no data migration is needed.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief comment in test_threshold_recalibration.py near the G7_BLOCKING constant (or in AGENTS.md) explaining the invariant: criteria blocked at exactly 0.90 go in PILOT_BLOCKING; criteria at other thresholds get a dedicated constant to avoid breaking the 0.90-parametrized assertion.
evidence: "G7 is deliberately NOT added to PILOT_BLOCKING because test_routing_posture_blocking_at_090 parametrizes over that dict asserting block_threshold == 0.90"
No mention of updating AGENTS.md or any design doc to record this new constant-naming convention for future criterion enablements at thresholds other than 0.90.
findings.finding: The new G7_BLOCKING constant (separate from PILOT_BLOCKING) establishes a new organizational pattern — per-criterion blocking constants at non-0.90 thresholds — with no guidance in AGENTS.md or a design note about when future criteria should create a new constant versus extend PILOT_BLOCKING or another existing structure.
findings.location: Approach section (4), 'G7 enters via a NEW G7_BLOCKING = {"G7": 0.85} constant added to the set-union expression'
scenarios: The next criterion enabled at 0.80 or 0.95 requires a new constant (e.g., NEW_BLOCKING); without guidance, the implementer may add it to PILOT_BLOCKING (breaking the 0.90 assertion) or invent another constant name, fragmenting the pattern.
A reviewer of a future criterion-enablement PR has no canonical reference for why some blocking criteria live in PILOT_BLOCKING and others have dedicated constants.
findings.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py, above the G7_BLOCKING definition, add: `# Criteria blocked at thresholds other than 0.90 get a dedicated constant (not PILOT_BLOCKING) to avoid breaking test_routing_posture_blocking_at_090's 0.90 assertion. Add future non-0.90 criteria here.`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether `G7_BLOCKING` needs to be a named constant (Rule-of-Three: 1 call-site) or whether inlining `| {"G7"}` directly in the set-union expression (matching how `{"T4", "prerequisite-consistency"}` is handled on the same line) is simpler and sufficient.
evidence: Plan (Testing section): 'G7 enters via a NEW `G7_BLOCKING = {"G7": 0.85}` constant added to the set-union expression (`... | set(PILOT_BLOCKING) | set(G7_BLOCKING) | ...`)'

test_threshold_recalibration.py line 163: `expected = LOWERED | set(PROMOTED) | set(PILOT_BLOCKING) | {"T4", "prerequisite-consistency"}` — single-criterion criteria like T4 and prerequisite-consistency are inlined directly, not extracted to named constants
G7_BLOCKING would have exactly 1 call-site in the codebase; Rule-of-Three requires >=3 call-sites for a named abstraction to not be premature
findings.finding: The new `G7_BLOCKING` constant in test_threshold_recalibration.py has exactly one call-site (`| set(G7_BLOCKING)` in `test_only_the_approved_and_prerequisite_criteria_are_blocking`), failing the Rule-of-Three bar for a named abstraction. The same intent could be expressed by inlining `| {"G7"}` directly in the set-union expression, which is how other single-criterion entries (`{"T4", "prerequisite-consistency"}`) are handled in that same assertion.
findings.location: Testing section / tests/unit/test_threshold_recalibration.py — `G7_BLOCKING` constant and its use in `test_only_the_approved_and_prerequisite_criteria_are_blocking`
scenarios: A reviewer sees LOWERED (5-item set), PROMOTED (4-item dict), PILOT_BLOCKING (3-item dict), and now G7_BLOCKING (1-item dict) and must understand why four named groupings exist and why G7 is in its own rather than PILOT_BLOCKING — the naming asymmetry adds cognitive overhead for a one-entry constant.
A future criterion at 0.85 might either need its own dict or cause confusion about whether to add it to G7_BLOCKING vs. a new constant.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `| set(G7_BLOCKING)` with `| {"G7"}` directly in the `expected = ...` expression in `test_only_the_approved_and_prerequisite_criteria_are_blocking`, and update the `EXPECTED_ROUTING` dict entry for G7 inline — no separate named constant needed for a single criterion at a unique threshold.

findings.finding: The plan asserts 'DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB stays strictly below every blocking block_threshold … pinned by tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py' (and decide.py:347-349 repeats this attribution). A search of tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py returns zero hits for 'DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB'. The actual pin is in tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py:142 (`assert DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB < min(blocking)`). test_impact_plan.py pins only UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB. This is an incorrect file citation for a load-bearing invariant: the Testing section says the test suite for this ticket runs test_impact_plan.py, so a developer relying on that file to confirm the invariant is live will be misled.
findings.location: Approach section (2), sentence 'DIVERGENCE_INCOMPLETE_CONTRIB, pinned strictly below every blocking threshold by tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py'
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach (2): replace 'pinned strictly below every blocking threshold by tests/unit/test_impact_plan.py' with 'pinned strictly below every blocking threshold by tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py'. In Testing: add `tests/unit/test_divergence_grade_split.py` to the pytest command line.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `git diff --exit-code docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` (or equivalent CI diff gate) to AC7's proving command so the no-diff assertion produces a concrete, non-zero-on-failure signal.
evidence: "docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md is regenerated (checked: `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` produces no diff on the committed tree)"

The regeneration command writes output but does not itself exit non-zero on a diff; a second command such as `git diff --exit-code docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is needed to produce a concrete pass/fail signal — that command is absent from both the AC and the Testing section.
findings.finding: AC7's proving command (`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide`) regenerates the file but the plan does not include the explicit diff-check invocation that would produce evidence of 'no diff on the committed tree', leaving the verification step implicit rather than concrete.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — last bullet (AC7) / Testing section
scenarios: An executor runs the regeneration command, sees no error output (the command exits 0 regardless of whether the file changed), and incorrectly concludes the criterion is satisfied without checking whether the committed file actually matches the freshly generated output.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC7 check text with: `(checked: run \'python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide\' then \'git diff --exit-code docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md\' exits 0 — any uncommitted diff fails CI)`
